 18th century, though cost remained prohibitive for common people.                                                     
                                                                                                                       
 Gas lighting revolutionized illumination in the 19th century. Coal gas provided bright, reliable light suitable for   
 streets, factories, and homes. Gas lamps proliferated in urban centers, enabling nighttime commerce and reducing      
 crime. However, gas was dangerous-leaks caused explosions and poisoning.                                              
                                                                                                                       
 Thomas Edison's incandescent bulb (1879) transformed civilization. Electric light was safer, cleaner, and ultimately  
 more efficient than gas or candles. Widespread electrification began in wealthy nations, enabling factories to        
 operate continuously and homes to extend productive hours. Electric lighting became a hallmark of modernity and       
 development.
